---
title: "Glossary"
---

AUC (area under the ROC curve)
: The probability that a randomly chosen defaulter is ranked riskier than a randomly chosen
  non-defaulter. 0.5 is a coin toss and 1 is perfect ranking. It measures ranking only, not
  whether the predicted probabilities are right, and it depends on the population it is
  measured on — so these pages never print one without its population.

Booked
: An applicant whose loan was made. The bank observes outcomes only for booked loans; the
  synthetic data give every applicant one, which is how these pages can compare the two
  populations.

Break-even rate
: The rate at which a loan's return on equity is zero: it covers the cost of funds, the
  expected loss and the operating cost, and earns nothing on the equity. A loan quoted below
  it loses money at its own rate (D6.3).

Capital charge
: The pre-tax return a loan must earn on the equity allocated to it for that equity to earn
  the ROE hurdle after tax: hurdle × capital ratio / (1 − tax rate), as a rate on exposure.
  The difference between the break-even and the hurdle-clearing rate (D6.3).

Capture (top-decile capture)
: The share of all events — here, deteriorations — that fall among the riskiest tenth of a
  population ranked by a model. A random ranking captures a tenth; capture divided by a tenth
  is the top-decile lift. Early Warning is gated on it, measured on held-out accounts (D7.5,
  D7.9).

Drawdown
: The share of a credit line a borrower actually uses. Line Increase assumes an increase is
  drawn at the account's current utilisation, so its incremental EAD is the increase times
  that utilisation; the ROE of each increase does not depend on the assumption, but every
  exposure figure does (D8.4, D8.7 finding 5).

EAD (exposure at default)
: The amount owed if the borrower defaults. Pricing here uses the requested amount;
  Line Increase uses the increase times the assumed drawdown.

Eligible
: Line Increase's offer: an account whose candidate probability clears the offer threshold,
  whose scorecard PD is within the risk-appetite ceiling, whose recommended amount is positive
  and whose incremental ROE clears the hurdle — all four. `candidates()` is the authority; a
  positive recommended amount alone is not an offer (D8.1).

Gate
: A committed minimum a model must meet on held-out data, asserted when it is trained and
  recomputed independently by `verify.py`. A gate is never relaxed to let a model pass; a
  failure is investigated and documented.

Holdout
: The share of the data set aside before fitting and used only to measure the model. A
  held-out metric estimates how the model ranks applicants it has not seen.

Hurdle-clearing rate
: The rate at which a loan's return on equity equals the hurdle: the break-even rate plus the
  capital charge. A loan quoted at or above it clears the hurdle; below it, it is mispriced
  (D6.3).

Incremental ROE
: The return on equity of an increase in a credit line, priced on its own by the pricing
  engine at the account's PD and quoted rate. Line Increase offers an increase only if it
  clears the hurdle; because every line of the waterfall is proportional to exposure, it
  equals the ROE of the existing loan at the same rate (D8.3).

IV (information value)
: A single-variable measure of how well a feature separates defaulters from non-defaulters,
  summed over its bins' weights of evidence. Convention reads values below {{< var monitoring.iv_useless >}} as
  unpredictive; IV says nothing about what a feature adds beside the others.

KS (Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistic)
: The largest gap between the cumulative score distributions of defaulters and
  non-defaulters. Like AUC it measures separation, and it too depends on the population.

Knockout
: A policy rule that declines an application whatever the model says — in adjudication, a
  debt-service coverage floor, public records, prior delinquencies or leverage (D5.3). Its
  reason is the rule, not the model.

LGD (loss given default)
: The share of the exposure lost if the borrower defaults, after recoveries. Here it is a
  market assumption in `shared.config.MARKET`, not an estimate.

Lift
: The default rate among the riskiest share of a population, ranked by a model, divided by
  the default rate of the whole population. A lift of 2 means the riskiest group defaults at
  twice the average rate. It depends on the share chosen, so these pages always name it. For
  Line Increase the event is the label and the share is the top fifth (top-quintile lift,
  D8.5).

Mispriced EAD
: The total exposure of the booked loans whose quoted rate is below their hurdle-clearing
  rate. It weights the mispricing measure by money rather than by loan count (D6.5).

PD (probability of default)
: The model's estimate that a borrower defaults over the outcome window. The scorecard's PD
  is what every downstream module consumes. The generator's *true* PD is on the leakage
  deny-list: it never exists at decision time.

Proxy
: A feature with no causal role of its own that carries real signal borrowed from one that
  has one — here, columns derived from annual revenue. It ranks, stably and monotonically,
  for someone else's reasons.

PR-AUC (area under the precision-recall curve)
: Average precision over every cut of a ranking: how rich in events the top of the list stays
  as it grows. A ranking with no information scores about the base rate, so it is read against
  the base rate, not against 0.5 as AUC is (D7.5).

PSI (population stability index)
: How far a distribution has moved between two samples, summed over bins. Convention reads
  below {{< var monitoring.psi_watch >}} as stable, {{< var monitoring.psi_watch >}} to
  {{< var monitoring.psi_act >}} as worth watching, and above {{< var monitoring.psi_act >}} as a shift
  that needs action.

RAROC (risk-adjusted return on capital)
: Return after expected loss, divided by the capital held against the risk. Reported by the
  pricing engine beside ROE.

ROE (return on equity)
: Net income on a loan divided by the equity allocated to it. The pricing engine solves for
  the rate at which a loan's ROE meets the hurdle.

SHAP (Shapley additive explanations)
: An attribution method that splits one prediction among the model's features, so that a base
  value plus the features' contributions equals the prediction (in log-odds, for a classifier).
  The adjudication model's reasons are SHAP values (D5.3); the policy layer's rule hits come
  first. It is exact in that sense, but how it shares
  credit between correlated features is a choice of the method, which a validator has to
  assess as well as the model.

Structural zero
: A feature the data generator gives no role in default at all. Any pattern it shows against
  default is sampling noise, however tidy the chart.

Tier (risk tier)
: In Early Warning, High, Medium or Low, from the model's probability against two cutoffs set
  at training as quantiles of that probability over the book. The cutoffs fix a review
  workload, not a probability limit (D7.3).

Trigger
: In Early Warning, a fixed rule that compares one behavioural feature with a threshold —
  high or rising utilisation, a late payment, falling deposits, frequent overdrafts — and
  names the account's warning sign. Triggers give a reason; the tier ranks (D7.3).

VIF (variance inflation factor)
: How much a coefficient's variance is inflated because its feature is predictable from the
  other features. High values mean the model cannot separate those features' effects.

WoE (weight of evidence)
: For one bin of a feature, the log of the ratio of that bin's share of non-defaulters to its
  share of defaulters. A scorecard replaces each raw value with its bin's WoE, so every
  point of the score traces back to one bin of one feature.
